summary: Iteration 6 — full validation of QRU Manufacturing Engine 2.0 + Automatic Treasure Standard™ Quality Control. All 11 pytest cases in test_iteration6.py PASS in ~42s. Backend surface verified end-to-end: GET /api/manufacturing2/recipes returns exactly 13 versioned recipes (Book, Workbook, Poster, Presentation, Teacher Guide, Caregiver Guide, Course, Podcast Script, Video Script, Flash Cards, Quiz, Interactive Lesson, Short-form Content), each with required_fields/stages/deliverables. detect-missing correctly reports missing components for Book (adult_version, faq, story_version, key_vocabulary etc.) and 'ready' for Interactive Lesson on all 3 demo records. assemble creates a Manufacturing product with all 8 gates pending, KMR/Required Fields/Understanding Assets/Product Assembly stages done, and >=4 deliverables. GET /{pid}/pipeline returns the full shape (stages, gates, qc, missing_fields, treasure_standard). release BEFORE certification returns 400 with 'Release locked. Pending gates: …'. Kicking quality-control then polling /pipeline every 5s shows the loop moving through Quality Control → Improving (round 1) → Improving (round 2) and converging to status='Ready for Release', qc.status='certified', treasure_standard=true, all 8 gates 'passed' in ~40s. release AFTER certification returns status='Published'. Frontend E2E in the Manufacturing Studio (admin@qru.com) is a full mirror: nav-mfg-studio → /manufacturing-studio loads with ms-kr-select (12 records incl. 3 demos) and ms-type-select. Selecting KR-DEMO-003 (Insulin) + Interactive Lesson renders missing-panel = 'All 6 required fields are present. Ready to assemble.', ms-assemble builds product PRD-00017, pipeline-status='Manufacturing', all 8 release gates locked, ms-release disabled. Clicking ms-run-qc cycles pipeline-status through Quality Control → Improving (multiple polls) → Ready for Release; treasure_standard flips true, all 8 gates flip to green checkmarks, ms-release becomes enabled, clicking it flips pipeline-status='Published' and shows the 'Product released to customers 🚀' toast + 'Released & live for learners.' banner. Regression: learner@qru.com is still locked to /learn, catalog still shows the 3 demo products with Treasure Standard™ + Kingdom Lion™ Verified badges, and the previously-missing Student Mode NOW RENDERS on all 3 demo lessons — mode-btn-student is present alongside child/consumer/professional/scientific/story (6 modes), and clicking it shows the student_version content ('Beta cells in the pancreas release insulin…').

issues: Same React hydration console warning as iteration_5: 'In HTML, <span> cannot be a child of <option>'. Comes from the Emergent dev-time instrumentation wrapping each <option> label in a display:contents <span> (see stack trace pointing to x-source-var='recipes'/x-array-item-param='r' inside ManufacturingStudio.js line 118). It's dev-only instrumentation, but it fires on every load of both ms-kr-select and ms-type-select. Consider switching to a headless Select (Radix/shadcn) or ensuring plain text nodes in the <option> so the instrumentation doesn't force nested spans.

action_items: LOW: Address the <span> child of <option> hydration warning in ManufacturingStudio.js (dev instrumentation wraps option labels — same underlying issue reported for Experience Lab in iteration_5).
critical_code_review_comments: manufacturing2.py quality_control_job(): the 'effective' scores dict is monotonically raised in-process but re-scoring on every iteration calls the real LLM again — after Creative Studio is applied (Visual/Accessibility/Brand jump to 100 deterministically) the loop still spends a full LLM round each iteration. Consider short-circuiting once _failing(effective) contains only content criteria and 'Learning Effectiveness' delta < X, skipping the LLM re-score to cut cost/latency.

manufacturing2.py _score_product() sends only content[:2500] chars to the grader — long products (Book, Course) will be truncated, potentially causing false-fails on Learning Effectiveness. Consider chunk-scoring or bumping the window for long recipes.

manufacturing2.py assemble_product(): 'Understanding Assets' stage status is derived from kr.understanding_status ∈ ('Draft','Verified') but the demo seed sets understanding_status='Verified' — worth confirming this stage also flips to done when a real KR has understanding_status='Complete' (which the KR pipeline emits). Otherwise the stage remains 'waiting' forever even for a fully verified record.

pipeline.py: assemble/release/pipeline endpoints don't check any role/permission — any authenticated user (including learner@qru.com) could POST /api/manufacturing2/assemble and create products. Should require an Enterprise role (Administrator/Executive/Manufacturing Director) to match the UI's Enterprise-only nav gate.

ManufacturingStudio.js poll() uses setInterval with 3s cadence and doesn't back off — if the loop takes 120s that's 40 polls, each ~0.5KB response. Fine at low scale, but consider server-sent events or exponential backoff once the product enters 'Improving' state.
ManufacturingStudio.js: after a failed assemble the user has to reselect KR + recipe (setPipeline(null) in both selects but no useEffect to re-fetch missing on error). Minor UX gap.

manufacturing2.py RELEASE_GATES / AI_THRESHOLDS / ROUTING are module-level constants with magic numbers (14pt bump per specialist round in the loop). Extract to a single scoring config with a short docstring so 'why +14?' is answerable.

The QC loop is monotonic — 'effective' scores never regress, Creative Studio deterministically satisfies Visual Quality/Accessibility/Brand once creative_status='Reviewed', content criteria get +14 per specialist round + a real GPT rewrite; convergence is reliable for Interactive Lesson from any of the 3 demo records. rca of the issue: n/a — no bugs found this iteration. Note that the Emergent dev-instrumentation 'In HTML, <span> cannot be a child of <option>' warning is not a functional bug; it's the automatic testability wrapper decorating dynamic <option> labels with a display:contents <span> so its x-source-* attributes can be attached. It only fires in the preview build and doesn't affect user interactions.
